senses.gloss: f.(b. h. חֲנֻכָּה; חָנַךְ)inauguration, dedication, festival of dedication; esp. Ḥănuckah, the eight days’ feast commemorating the rededication of the Temple after its desecration under Antioch Epiphanes, lasting from the 25ᵗʰ of Kislev to the second (or third) of Tebeth.
units: <cite ref="Shabbat 21b:10">Sabb. 21ᵇ</cite> <he>מאי ח׳</he> why dedication ceremonies (illumination)? <cite ref="Shabbat 21b:5">Ib.</cite> <he>מצות ח׳</he> the proper observation of Ḥ. (illumination).
<cite ref="Shabbat 21b:12">Ib.</cite> <he>נר ח׳</he> the lights kindled on Ḥ.—

<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 2:1">Pesik. R. s. 2</cite> <he>חֲנוּכַּת שמים וארץ</he> the dedication of heaven and earth (by illumination, ref. to <cite ref="Genesis 1:18">Gen. I, 18</cite>); <he>ח׳ החומה</he> the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem (<cite ref="Nehemiah 12:27">Neh. XII, 27</cite>); <he>ח׳ הכהנים</he> the dedication (illumination) instituted by the Asmonean priests; a. fr.—Pl. <he>חֲנוּכּוֹת</he>.
